$comment: Blocks retired from public/content/ under hard rule 1a of the visual compaction brief, and the
figure that took over each one's job.
RULE 1a, IN FULL: an ASCII or box-drawing diagram, a pseudo-table inside a code block, a stack
of near-identical cards or a restated 'summary' table may be deleted ONCE a figure renders the
same facts. A visual takes over the job only when it shows every fact, number, tier label and
source the text it replaces carried — and every figure keeps a 'View the data' disclosure, which ships OPEN and is closed by script (see components/PrintSafeDisclosures.tsx),
generated from its data file, so the numbers stay on the page and stay in the printed PDF.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. scripts/verify-content-integrity.mjs compares every body line against the
baseline and fails the build on anything that moved, which is exactly right: the restructure
moved body text, it did not rewrite it. A retirement is the one thing this brief authorises
that the guard cannot tell apart from a quiet deletion. Declaring it costs one entry and a
sentence saying which figure carries the facts — the same bargain notation-rewrites.json
strikes for prose, and scripts/figure-migrations.json for figures leaving the markdown.
`facts` is not decoration. It is the checklist the figure is held to, and Phase 8's report
itemises the words retired against it. If a fact listed here is not visible in the figure or in
its 'View the data' table, the retirement is not authorised and the block goes back.

`blocks` is how many fenced blocks the entry retires — omit it for one. The three §3.6 section banners are one entry covering three blocks, so the fence-delimiter allowance has to count blocks and not entries.

facts: The question: Governor Malombe's 2027 constitutional status under Article 180(7)
Branch A's reading: interrupted terms count toward the cumulative limit of two terms
Branch B's reading: only contiguous terms or uninterrupted service triggers the lifetime limit

retirements.was: A box-drawing table headed DPA 2019 STATUTORY COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST — six legal requirements, each with its operational campaign implementation.
facts: Lawful basis for processing (Sec 30): explicit affirmative opt-in before any bulk political SMS
Purpose limitation (Sec 25): contact details will NEVER be sold, shared or repurposed
Data minimisation (Sec 25): only necessary operational fields; no unnecessary biometric or sensitive data
Mandatory opt-out (Sec 34): EVERY broadcast message must carry an immediate, free opt-out — 'Reply STOP to OptOut'
Data security and encryption (Sec 41): RBAC, end-to-end AES-256 encryption, local cloud hosting
Right to rectify / erasure (Sec 40): a direct automated USSD/SMS command for complete profile deletion

retirements.was: A box-drawing chain headed THREE-TIER ESCALATION PROTOCOL — three levels with their issues, resolution authority and rule.
facts: Level 1, operational resolution under 1 hour: logistics delays, vendor equipment failure, routine social rumours; the respective functional lead resolves and logs in the Daily Pulse Report

Level 2, strategic & scope escalation under 2 hours: scope overruns, a competitor attack requiring a major change in media weighting, a constituency coordinator dispute; the Campaign Manager makes a binding operational determination

Level 3, governance, coalition & red-line escalation under 4 hours: Wiper leadership alignments, major endorsements or defections, litigation and legal threats, fundamental manifesto revisions; Dr. Makali Mulu and the Strategic Advisory Board, candidate delivers the final executive directive
retirements.note: Numbered because escalation is ordered: a level 1 issue unresolved inside the hour becomes a level 2 issue and the authority changes with it. Each level names who decides and what they must do, which is what makes it a protocol rather than a list.

retirements.was: A pseudo-table headed RAPID RESPONSE DECISION MATRIX — four threat severities with definition and impact threshold, strategic response protocol and turnaround SLA.
facts: Level 1 negligible: isolated comment under 50 views, fringe blog or anonymous — IGNORE / PASSIVE MONITOR, log to the intelligence feed, do NOT amplify or refute; no public response, continued observation for velocity changes
Level 2 moderate: rumour active in 3+ ward WhatsApp groups or one market centre baraza — CONTAIN AT WARD LEVEL with a 45s WhatsApp Kikamba voice note and fact-check card; under 30 minutes

Level 3 high: morning vernacular radio mention, prominent rival press conference — HIGH-VELOCITY REBUTTAL, live studio call-in or signed media card; under 15 minutes call-in, under 45 minutes fact-check infographic

Level 4 critical: coordinated county-wide smear, national TV story, legal or regulatory threat — EXECUTIVE CRISIS COUNTER, candidate live broadcast or constituency lead joint press; under 15 minutes war room, under 1 hour official press, under 2 hours 2G ward SMS
retirements.note: LEVEL 1'S PROTOCOL IS TO DO NOTHING, with an explicit instruction not to amplify or refute. Every Kikamba framing is transcribed character for character, diacritics included — ĩ, ũ and the apostrophe in kũtelemw'a — because §7.3.2 forbids machine translation of exactly this material and a normalised vowel is what that rule exists to prevent.
